From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:41:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: live chat — major lag during promo push

Quick triage notes (15:41 PDT):
- Observed: p95 ~ 1.2s (ok) but p99 jumped to 9–14s during 14:58–15:10 window. Error rate for streaming connections increased from 0.2% -> 2.9% (WS disconnects and 502s on gateway).
- Root suspects: connection backpressure on the SSE router + queue buildup in connector pool. Autoscaler for stream-workers didn't respond fast enough due to our 5-min stabilization window; new connections are queuing behind long-running responses (longer generation times during peak prompt lengths).
- Evidence: attached grafana snapshot and tail of streaming logs (connection backlog metric spiked to 620).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (can apply in the next 10–20m):
1) Temporarily increase stream-worker pool by +40% (manual scale override).
2) Reduce default max tokens for this tenant by 30% for streaming sessions (config override) to reduce per-request generation time.
3) Enable polling fallback for new connections that hit backlog >250 (rate-limited).

If Dev agrees, we can run 1 and 3 now; 2 needs ops approval and coordination with product (risk: slight quality drop). I'll prepare a short customer-facing note.

-Rishi
Head of Serving Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments: grafana-promotions-2026-08-19.png, tail-stream-logs.txt (in support-logs-20260819.zip)

I can run the manual scale and enable polling fallback now. A few operational notes:
- Manual scale: will take ~6 minutes to provision and drain concurrently. We'll rotate pods to avoid connection drops by using sticky handshake to new workers.
- Polling fallback: toggle on gateway level; clients will reconnect as polling when SSE handshake fails. This will increase latency slightly for some users but avoid timeouts.
- Regarding token cap: we need Product sign-off; propose a targeted tenant override only for QuickSale for the next 2 hours.

I'll kick off the scale and enable fallback in the next 8m and post results. If backlog doesn't drop, plan B is rolling back to the previous model variant (we rolled a heavier LM variant 48h ago).

-Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@quicksale.com>
Cc: Luis Ortega <ops@quicksale.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Update: QuickSale live chat — interim mitigation deployed

Samantha — quick update and apologies for the disruption. Summary:
- What happened: during your 3pm promo blast we saw an unexpected burst that drove streaming p99 to ~12s and caused increased disconnects. Root cause appears to be connection backlog + recent heavier model variant increasing per-request generation time.
- What we did (interim, already applied): manual scale +40% of stream workers; enabled polling fallback for new connections; applied tenant-level max token cap (30% reduction) for the next 2 hours.
- Impact observed: backlog dropped from 620 -> 90 within 9 minutes; p99 returned to 1.5–2.0s and error rate back down to ~0.35%.
- Next steps: 1) We'll keep the temporary cap for 2 hours and remove it afterwards unless you prefer otherwise. 2) We'll investigate autoscaler tuning and prepare a playbook for promo events (scheduled scaling, model-variant guardrails). 3) We'll follow up with a credit proposal for the affected window.

We're very sorry for the disruption — appreciate you flagging it early. If you'd like, we can set up a 30-minute postmortem tomorrow to review the playbook and ensure we have runbooks for future promotions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: support-logs-20260819.zip
